statement: A based ambient-null plane loop commuting with an arbitrary specified operator group has a based filling in that same centralizer, fixing its nonopen locus pointwise, when the nonopen locus of the loop-generated action is zero-dimensional. All operator dimensions are included. The exact comparison is that restriction from sphere homeomorphisms preserving a nonempty compact zero-dimensional set setwise to homeomorphisms of its complement is an isomorphism of topological groups, with unique end extension as inverse. Connected based families fix every end individually. The same conclusion descends to every connected admissible surface when the nonopen locus of the based plane lift is zero-dimensional.
depends_on: Explicit finite disjoint Jordan-disk covers of compact zero-dimensional planar sets; exact component-system construction of the end compactification; compact-open and inverse convergence proof for extension; C30 full local centralizer properness; C32 ambient-null restriction; C33 intrinsic proper-operator centralizer filling; actual universal-cover lifting and deck descent
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison for the zero-dimensional nonopen locus
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The deleted set is not assumed locally connected. The finite Jordan covers and both directions of the group topology comparison are proved. The full sphere group preserves the end remainder setwise, while a connected based filling fixes each end individually, including the plane's specified infinity. Every operator label and the actual restriction kernel are retained.
notes: Finite clopen partitions and small planar regular neighborhoods yield pairwise disjoint Jordan-disk covers of arbitrarily small mesh. Refining these covers gives a connected compact exhaustion whose complementary components identify the actual ends one by one with the deleted set. For a convergent family of homeomorphisms and inverses, compactness of the union of inverse images of one compact core supplies a larger compact core; one reference point in each of its finitely many complementary components then controls all end images. This proves uniform extension convergence on the sphere, including inverses. A zero-dimensional nonopen locus is pointwise fixed by the path-connected generated group, and its complement is the unique open orbit. C30-C33 supply an intrinsic filling; the exact extension isomorphism makes it a global filling. Universal-cover uniqueness and open-quotient descent retain every original surface and deck label. The result does not provide the remaining extension across positive-dimensional fixed sets or nonfixed one-dimensional frontier orbits; C12 remains open.
sources: C_BeguinCrovisierLeRoux2020: verified publisher metadata; arXiv:1610.00686v2 Proposition 1.5 and Appendix A.1 as primary background for end extension. The full topological group comparison required here is proved in C66.
